title: The schedule door refuses a Library item that is not an export
body:
## Summary
realSchedule and fixtureSchedule admitted any Library item on a video channel; the youtube adapter refuses non-exports at its tick.

## Description
app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/real.ts realSchedule passed any item library_docs holds to createSlot; lib/producers/publish.ts:70 youtubeAdapter.plan refuses `<item> is not an export; youtube publishes exports`. Both sides now refuse at the door in that sentence (real.ts exportOnly).

## Flow
- schedule a video:clip item on youtube -> slot made -> fails at the tick
- after: refused at the door, verbatim

## Expected impact
The operator cannot make a slot that can only fail.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a slot that can only fail is refused when made
Before: 0 of 2 sides refuse
After: 2 of 2; 2 new cases red on HEAD, green after
Method: gate - tests/next-server/floor.test.ts, floor-real.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: A level whose port call rejects says so instead of staying busy
body:
## Summary
Six Server Action calls in _floor ran `.then(onAnswer)` with no rejection arm; a rejected action left the slot level armed and busy for good.

## Description
SlotLevel.tsx run/detail/conflict re-read, ScheduleLevel.tsx send/items, Composers.tsx useEstimate. Registry async-ui-states/action-busy-states: 'one thrown error leaves the button spinning forever'. New _floor/settle.ts maps a rejection to an `unavailable` refusal.

## Flow
- press Publish now with the server gone -> rejection unhandled -> armed ref stays set -> every later press silently refused
- after: the refusal is drawn and the level disarms

## Expected impact
A dropped network no longer bricks the slot level or the schedule sheet until reload.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - rejection handled on every port call
Before: 0 of 6
After: 6 of 6; floor-settle.test.ts 3 cases, seeded red (2 failing)
Method: gate
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A fixture slot published dry holds nothing, as the slot store says
body:
## Summary
The fixture's rail mapping dropped `dry` and its clash list counted every published slot, so a dry publish-now held its export forever.

## Description
fixture.ts railOfRow (a second copy of real.ts railOfSlot) and HOLDS diverged from @gt/ui schedule.ts holds / the slots_one_holder index. Now railOfRow is railOfSlot over the fixture row and the clash check is holds().

## Flow
- publish-now a fixture slot (dry) -> schedule the same export on that channel -> refused 'already on tiktok'
- after: scheduled

## Expected impact
The fixture universe the cx screens photograph agrees with the real one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, two sides agree
Before: dry respected on 1 of 2 sides; 2 copies of the rail map
After: 2 of 2; 1 copy; new case red on HEAD and with only the rail half fixed
Method: gate
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A slot's record and its verbs stop reading every slot
body:
## Summary
real.ts ctx() listed the whole slot table for every record open and verb, only for lastChannel which they never read.

## Description
Registry bounded-enumeration. ctx(withRows) reads rows only for realSlots.

## Flow
- open a slot record with 3000 slots in the store -> 25 ms, linear in history
- after: 0.27 ms

## Expected impact
Record opens and verbs stay flat as the calendar's history grows.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - per-record cost independent of history
Before: N=300 2.04/1.92 ms; N=3000 25.36/22.92 ms (record/stale verb)
After: N=300 0.77/0.37; N=3000 0.27/0.21
Method: probe - temp kernel seeded with N slots, 40 timed calls each side
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The Projects shelf reads the kernel's projects instead of drawing only a door
instrument: a floor.test case over a readShelf `projects` read (fixture side: the produce fixture's projects; real: listProjects over a temp kernel) asserting count + rows, then cx-capture `floor` to see the column; seed red on HEAD shelf.ts (no projects key)
body:
## Summary
The video lane's ratified column draws a head and a /projects door with no count, though the produce port now lists projects.

## Description
shelf.ts video branch and LaneCells.tsx ShelfBody's last return; shelfCount returns null for video, which Floor.tsx reads as `?? 0` for laneRows (row shrinks to .7fr) but `?? 1` for shelfEmpty - two answers for 'cannot count'. Reading serverProduce().listProjects() into the shelf gives the column a real count and rows (SHELF_ROWS bound) and removes the null branch.

## Flow
- page load -> video lane shelf shows only a door
- build: shelf.ts projects read via serverProduce().listProjects, bounded; LaneCells video branch draws ShelfList; shelfCount(video) = projects total

## Expected impact
Operator sees ratified video work on the Floor like the other three lanes. Could break: the produce real side's listProjects cost on every Floor render.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the fourth shelf states what it holds
Before: video shelf: 0 rows, no count; 2 contradictory null readings
After: predicted: N rows, a count, 1 reading
Method: simulation - three lanes already do it (styles, posts, takes); no instrument built this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: The rail and the month carry every slot the calendar ever held
instrument: the scratch probe from 4b58e4c7 (temp kernel, N slots) extended to time realSlots and measure JSON.stringify(data.slots).length at N=300/3000; arm B windows listSlots to [month-1, month+2] plus unsettled states and the month fetches a turned page through a port verb
body:
## Summary
realSlots lists the whole slot table unbounded and ships it to the client on every render and every live-feed refresh.

## Description
real.ts realSlots -> listSlots(store) with no from/to/limit (packages/kernel/src/slots/read.ts listSlotsIn); Floor.tsx hands data.slots to the rail, the month and the schedule form. Registry bounded-enumeration: an enumeration without a bound grows with history. The month turns pages client-side, so a window needs a port read per page.

## Flow
- a year of daily slots on 3 channels -> ~1100 RailSlots re-serialized per router.refresh
- build: window the read, add `month(ym)` to the CalendarPort, keep unsettled rows always

## Expected impact
Floor render cost and payload stop growing with publishing history. Could break: the month's past pages and the schedule form's held-item check.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - bounded calendar read
Before: unbounded (rows = all slots); not timed this round
After: predicted bounded by the window
Method: simulation - instrument named, unbuilt
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
drain_note: needs a month(ym) CalendarPort verb across 5 files; XL-ish

title: At phone width the Floor's three columns get 78 px between them
instrument: CX_BASE=... node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs floor out.png --width 390 plus a scrollWidth/clientWidth overflow read of [data-component=Floor]; arm B stacks the calendar rail under the lanes below ~700px (the breakpoint Floor.module.css already uses for .foundryCell)
body:
## Summary
The Floor grid keeps the calendar column at its 260 px floor at every width, leaving ~130 px for the lane label and three columns at 390 px.

## Description
Floor.module.css .floor grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) var(--cal-w); tokens.css --cal-w: clamp(260px,19vw,340px); --cols: 52px + three fr columns; the only media query is .foundryCell's at 700px. 390 - 260 - 52 = 78 px for Foundry, Weir and shelf together.

## Flow
- open /floor on a 390 px viewport -> three columns of ~26 px each, colheads clipped (white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden)
- build: a <=700px rule that moves the rail below the lanes

## Expected impact
The Floor is usable on a phone. Could break: the rail's open/close animation and the month layer's anchoring; part of the fix is packages/ui (out of scope).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - phone viewport usable
Before: 78 px across three columns at 390 px (arithmetic from the tokens)
After: predicted full width per column when stacked
Method: simulation - no dev server allowed in a round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Every Floor re-read re-prices each open lane's composer
instrument: a vitest case over useEstimate's dependency rule extracted as a pure key (lane, choice, queue revision) counting composerReceipt calls across 3 refreshes with an unchanged queue: 12 today (4 lanes x 3) vs 0 under a queue-revision key
body:
## Summary
useEstimate's effect depends on `epoch` = data.now, so every router.refresh (live feed, 30 s backstop) sends one composerReceipt Server Action per unfolded lane.

## Description
Composers.tsx useEstimate deps [port, lane, choice, epoch]; Floor.tsx passes epoch={data.now}. The header says this is on purpose ('a launch elsewhere moves the queue'), so the cheaper key is the queue's own revision, not the clock.

## Flow
- leave the Floor open -> 4 receipt reads per refresh, whatever changed

## Expected impact
Fewer server reads on an idle Floor. Could break: an estimate that should move with the queue and does not.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - receipt reads per idle refresh
Before: 4 per refresh (read from the deps)
After: predicted 0 when the queue did not move
Method: simulation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
